source_text: Ποῖος σωρὸς μείζων, ἀχύρου ἢ τοῦ σίτου; Ὅταν γὰρ ἔλθῃ ὁ γεωργὸς ἐν τῷ πτύῳ διακαθᾶραι τὴν ἅλωνα, τὸ ἄχυρον κοῦφον ὂν εὐκόλως ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀερίου πνεύματος μεταφέρεται, ὁ δὲ σῖτος ἐν ταὐτῷ μένει. Ἴδετε πάλιν τὴν εἰς θάλασσαν βαλλομένην σαγήνην· μὴ πάντα ἃ συνάγει ἄχρηστά ἐστιν; Οὕτω καὶ τὰ παρόντα. Πῶς οὖν θέλετε ταῦτα πάσχειν ἡμᾶς, ὡς δικαίους ἢ ὡς ἀδίκους; Εἰ μὲν ὡς ἀδίκους, πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ ὑμεῖς αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἔργοις ἄδικοι ἐλεγχόμενοι τὰ αὐτὰ πείσεσθε; Εἰ δὲ ὡς δικαίους, τῶν δικαίων πασχόντων ποίαν ὑμεῖς ἐλπίδα ἔχετε; Εἰ γὰρ ὁ δίκαιος μόλις σώζεται, ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται; Κρίσις γὰρ τῷ κόσμῳ ἐπίκειται, περὶ ἧς πεπληροφορήμεθα διὰ πολλῶν. Ἐγὼ μὲν καὶ ἀποδημήσας καὶ ἅπασαν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν περιελθὼν γῆν περάσας τε τὸν Ἰορδάνην ἐθεασάμην γῆν ἕως τοῦ νῦν μαρτυροῦσαν τὴν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γενομένην αὐτῇ ὀργήν, δι᾽ ἃς ἐποίουν οἱ κατοικοῦντες αὐτὴν ἁμαρτίας, ξενοκτονοῦντες, ξενηλατοῦντες, βιαζόμενοι. Εἶδον καπνὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἕως τοῦ νῦν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ γῆν πυρὶ τετεφρωμένην, ἄμοιρον παντὸς καρποῦ καὶ πάσης ὑγρᾶς οὐσίας. Εἶδον καὶ Θάλασσαν Νεκράν, ὕδωρ ὑπηλλαγμένον καὶ ἔξω τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν φόβῳ θείῳ ἀτονῆσαν καὶ τρέφειν ζῷον μὴ δυνάμενον, καὶ τὸν ἐναλλόμενον εἰς αὐτὴν ὑπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος ἐκβαλλόμενον εἰς ἄνω, καὶ κατέχειν ἀνθρώπου σῶμα παρ᾽ ἑαυτῇ μὴ δυναμένην· ὑποδέξασθαι γὰρ ἄνθρωπον οὐ θέλει, ἵνα μὴ δι᾽ ἄνθρωπον πάλιν ἐπιτιμηθῇ. Καὶ ταῦτα μακρὰν ὑμῶν ὄντα λέγω. Ὑμεῖς ὁρᾶτε καὶ διηγεῖσθε Λυδίας γῆν Δεκαπόλεως κατακαυμένην πυρὶ καὶ προκειμένην εἰς δεῦρο ὑπόδειγμα ἀσεβῶν, Αἴτνης καὶ Σικελίας καὶ Λυκίας καὶ τῶν νήσων ῥοιγδούμενον πῦρ. Εἰ δὲ καὶ ταῦτα πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀφ᾽ ὑμῶν, κατανοήσατε τοῦ θερμοῦ ὕδατος τὴν χρῆσιν, λέγω δὴ τοῦ ἀναβλύζοντος ἐκ γῆς, καὶ νοήσατε πόθεν ἀνάπτεται ἢ πόθεν πυροῦται, εἰ μὴ ἐκβαῖνον διὰ ὑπογαίου πυρός. Λόγετε δὲ καὶ ἐκπυρώσεις μερικὰς καὶ ἐξυδατώσεις, ὡς ὑμεῖς ἐπὶ Δευκαλίωνος ἢ ὡς ἡμεῖς ἐπὶ Νῶε. Μερικὰ γίνεται, ἵνα ἐκ τῶν ἐπὶ μέρους τὰ καθόλου γνωσθῇ. Διὸ δὴ μαρτυρόμεθα ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς μελλούσης διὰ πυρὸς γίνεσθαι κρίσεως ὑπὸ θεοῦ διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τοῖς λεγομένοις θεοῖς ὑμῶν οὐ λατρεύομεν καὶ τῇ εἰκόνι τῇ χρυσῇ οὐ προσκυνοῦμεν.
pass_a_gloss: Which heap is greater, that of chaff or that of wheat; for when the farmer comes with the winnowing tool to clean out the threshing floor, the chaff being light is easily carried off by the airy wind, but the wheat remains in the same place. See again the net cast into the sea; are not all the things it gathers useless. So also are present things. How then do you want us to suffer these things, as righteous or as unrighteous; for if as unrighteous, how will not you also, convicted as unrighteous by those very deeds, suffer the same things; but if as righteous, when the righteous suffer what hope do you have; for if the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and sinner appear. For judgment impends over the world, about which we have been fully assured through many things. For I both went abroad and traveled through all the land of Judea and crossed the Jordan and saw land until now bearing witness to the wrath that came upon it from God, for the sins which its inhabitants did, murdering strangers, expelling strangers, doing violence. I saw smoke still going up from it until now and land burnt to ash by fire, without share in any fruit and all moist substance. And I saw the Dead Sea, water changed and enfeebled outside what is according to nature by divine fear and unable to nourish a living creature, and the one who jumps into it being cast out upward by the water, and it not able to hold a human body with itself; for it does not want to receive a human, lest it be rebuked again on account of a human. And these things, being far from you, I say. You see and recount the burnt land of Lydia of the Decapolis lying before you until now as an example to the ungodly, the roaring fire of Aetna and Sicily and Lycia and the islands. But if even these are far distant from you, consider the use of hot water, I mean that which gushes up from the earth, and understand from where it is kindled or from where it is heated, if not as it comes forth through underground fire. And reckon also partial conflagrations and partial inundations, as you tell of in the time of Deucalion or as we tell in the time of Noah. Partial things happen, in order that from the things in part the universal things may be known. Therefore we testify to you concerning the coming judgment through fire by God through his Word Jesus Christ. And for this reason we do not serve your so-called gods and we do not worship the golden image.
pass_b_english: Which heap is the greater, the heap of chaff or the heap of wheat? When the farmer comes with his winnowing fork to clean out the threshing floor, the chaff, since it is light, is easily carried away by the gust of air, but the wheat stays in the same place. Consider again the net thrown into the sea; is not everything it gathers worthless? So it is also with present things. How then do you want us to suffer these things, as unrighteous people or as righteous people? If as unrighteous, how will you yourselves escape suffering the same, since you stand convicted as unrighteous by those very deeds. But if as righteous, when the righteous suffer, what hope do you have? For if the righteous person is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear (1 Peter 4:18). For judgment hangs over the world, and we have been fully persuaded of it by many proofs.

For I myself traveled abroad and passed through the whole land of Judea and crossed the Jordan, and I saw a land that even to this day bears witness to the wrath of God that came upon it for the sins its dwellers committed, for they murdered strangers and drove strangers away and did violence. I saw smoke still rising from it to this day, and a land burned to ash by fire, deprived of all fruit and of all moisture. I also saw the Dead Sea, its water altered and grown feeble against nature by divine fear, unable to nourish any living creature, casting back upward by the water the one who plunges into it, and unable to keep a human body within itself. For it refuses to receive a human being, lest it be rebuked again because of a human being. These things I mention, though they are far from you. You yourselves see and speak of the fire-scorched land of Lydia of the Decapolis lying before you to this day as a warning to the ungodly, and the roaring fire of Aetna and Sicily and Lycia and the islands. And if even these are far away from you, consider the use of hot water, I mean the water that gushes up from the earth, and understand where it is kindled and where it is heated, if not as it passes through subterranean fire. Consider also partial burnings and partial floodings, such as you tell of in the days of Deucalion and we tell of in the days of Noah. Such partial events occur so that from the particular the universal may be known. Therefore we solemnly testify to you of the coming judgment through fire by God through his Word Jesus Christ. And for this reason we do not serve your so-called gods, and we do not worship the golden image.
